instructions: Answer all questions. For fill‑in‑the‑blank and short‑answer, use one word, letter, or number only.
title: Discounting an Interest-Bearing Note before Maturity

options: Borrowing more money from the bank
Selling the note to a bank before maturity
Paying off the note early
Extending the maturity date
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Discounting means selling the note to a bank before maturity.
questions.prompt: When a company discounts a note, it is:
The fee the bank charges for discounting a note is called the ___ discount.
Note face $5,000, interest rate 6%, full term 60 days. Find maturity value. (number only, no $)
The discount period is the time from:
options: The date of the note to the discount date
The discount date to the maturity date
The date of the note to the maturity date
The discount date to the date of the note
hints: It's the remaining life of the note.
The bank holds the note during this period.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The discount period runs from the discount date to the maturity date.

questions.prompt: Bank discount = Maturity value × Discount rate × (Discount period / ___)
hints: The number of days in the ordinary interest year.

questions.prompt: Maturity value $10,000, discount rate 9%, discount period 40 days. Find bank discount. (two decimals, no $)

options: MV + Bank discount
MV − Bank discount
Face value + Interest
Face value − Bank discount
questions.prompt: Proceeds from discounting are calculated as:
A note with face $4,000, 5% interest, 90 days is discounted after 30 days at 8%. Find the discount period in days. (number only)
hints: Full term = 90 days, discount date is after 30 days.

questions.feedbackIfWrong: Contingent liability is the discounter's obligation to pay the bank if the maker defaults.
options: It ends when the note is discounted
It is the discounter's obligation to pay if the maker defaults
It equals the bank discount
It is paid by the bank
questions.prompt: Which statement about contingent liability is true?
If the maker defaults on a discounted note, the discounter must pay the bank the ___ value.
hints: It's the amount due at maturity.

questions.prompt: A company discounted a note and received $2,900 proceeds. The maturity value was $3,000. If the maker defaults, what is the company's net cash loss? (number only, no $)

options: Because the face value is unknown
Because the bank will collect the maturity value at maturity
Because the discount rate applies to interest only
Because the face value includes interest
questions.prompt: Why is the bank discount calculated on the maturity value instead of the face value?
questions.feedbackIfWrong: The bank will collect the maturity value, so the discount is based on that amount.
hints: Think about what the bank ultimately receives.
Maturity value is the total repayment.
